reasoning: Both outputs produce a valid RecipeManager skill with proper structure, YAML frontmatter, workflows, and examples. However, Output A is significantly more thorough and well-designed. It includes two Standards files (RecipeSchema.md and DataStorage.md) that provide deep, actionable specifications: a full YAML recipe schema with typed fields, allowed units, ingredient categories, validation rules, a normalization lookup table with synonym mappings, unit conversion tables, and duplicate detection procedures. Its workflows are more detailed -- AddRecipe includes URL fetching, slug generation, duplicate checking, schema validation, and error handling; SearchByIngredient has three-tier matching (exact, substring, base-word), multiple search modes (ALL/ANY/STRICT), and pantry staple exclusions; GenerateShoppingList includes fuzzy recipe matching, unit conversion with a complete conversion table, pantry staple identification, and follow-up actions. Output A's SkillIntent provides a full design philosophy section explaining structured data over freeform text, write-time normalization, flat files over databases, and ingredient-centric organization. Its SKILL.md also includes Architecture Notes explaining the flat-file tradeoff. Output B is competent -- it has valid structure, good examples, and a solid SkillIntent with design decisions table -- but its workflows are thinner (SearchByIngredient uses simpler percentage-based matching without tiered matching or search modes) and it lacks the Standards files that give Output A its actionable depth. Output A created 7 content files to Output B's 5, and the additional files are substantive, not padding.
